Yes, but don't do that just yet. 

Godot likes PRs to have only a single commit, to keep the Git history cleaner. There are two ways to do that:
- Amend your PR as you work on it, described [here](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/contributing/workflow/pr_workflow.html#modifying-a-pull-request).
- Make fixup commits (including committing suggestions using the GitHub UI), then at the end "squash" all your commits together, described [here](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/contributing/workflow/pr_workflow.html#the-interactive-rebase).

You can use either, or both. Usually I find it easier to use amend, and I manually copy and paste suggestions from GitHub to my text editor. But you can also use the GitHub UI to "commit suggestion" and then squash at the end after all the changes are made. It's up to you.
